tekst: Hello. I'm attaché. I read your inbox, sort it and prepare your replies with Claude. You decide what happens, and you always press send yourself.
There are three views: To do, Planning and Tidy up. The numbers show how much is waiting in each.
This line shows your day. You see what is on now or next, this week's deadlines, and email that has been waiting.
I put each email in one of four groups: Reply, Decide, Do and Check yourself.
When you open an email, you see at the top what it asks of you, and the first lines of the message.
Where I don't know something, I ask you. Choose an answer, and I write it into the draft.
Any spot that still needs filling in stays highlighted, and Send shows how many are left.
When you reply, the tasks from this email go to Planning.
With Reply in Mail, I prepare your reply in Apple Mail, and you send it from there. When you click Done, I file the email in the right folder, and you can undo that.
Some emails ask for a decision. If you accept a review, I add the review itself to Planning. If you decline, I leave it out.
Some senders never reach Claude. You answer those yourself.
I never send email by myself. Before a message goes to Claude, I replace student numbers and IBANs with codes.
You can do everything from the keyboard. Press the question mark to see every shortcut.
In Planning, you drag a task into your day, or you select it and move it with the arrow keys.
Tidy up lists newsletters and email for your information. You can archive or file them all at once.
The gear opens Settings, with the theme, the layout and the privacy options.
That's the introduction. You can watch it again under Settings. attaché. Minding the details.
